meaning: to put, to place; to turn on
title: Spanish Verb Poner Practice: Forms, Ponerse and Self-Correcting Quiz
description: Practice the Spanish verb poner: pongo, the preterite puse, ponerse, ten questions that correct themselves and a short reading. Free, no login.
intro: Poner means «to put», but it also means to turn on a device, to set the table and, as ponerse, to put on clothes or to become. Learn its forms and practice with instant feedback.

quiz.why: One person turned it on: puso.

paragraphs: El lunes, Diego se despertó tarde. Se puso los jeans de ayer, se puso una sudadera y salió de su cuarto corriendo. Su mamá ya había puesto el desayuno en la mesa, pero él no tenía tiempo para comer. Puso dos tostadas en una servilleta y las metió en la mochila.

En el autobús se dio cuenta de un problema: no se había puesto los tenis, sino las pantuflas. Se puso rojo de vergüenza. Su amiga Camila se rio y le dijo: «Tranquilo, nadie mira tus pies». Desde ese día, Diego pone la alarma diez minutos antes.

mistakes.why: The yo form of poner has g: pongo.
The preterite of poner uses the stem pus-.

mistakes.wrong: Pongo mi chaqueta (to put it on).
mistakes.why: Putting on clothes uses ponerse, and Spanish uses la, not mi.

heritage: Heritage speakers often say «pusistes» or «ponido». In writing, the forms are pusiste and puesto (the participle). Also check that puse and puso have no accent. Write about a morning when everything went wrong, using poner and ponerse at least five times.
teacher: Teachers: the reading is a funny morning routine with many uses of poner and ponerse. Ask students to find each one and decide whether it means to put, to put on or to become. Then they write their own morning-disaster story.
